chunks: Ahmad ibn Isha narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Kahili, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who gave a man wealth as a mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), and designated for him a specific portion of the profit. The mudarib (partner managing the trade) purchased goods and placed them in the capital. He said: 'Upon the mudarib is [liable for] the loss [in value] to the extent of the profit designated for him.' This does not contradict the earlier reports, because this report is understood to be when the wealth is a partnership between them, in which case the profit and loss are shared between them. The term 'mudarabah' was applied to it metaphorically, or because the wealth was entirely from his side, even if he made some of it a debt upon himself to validate the partnership. And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the liability of the managing partner in a mudarabah partnership if a specific profit share is designated?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the distribution of loss in a mudarabah contract when a fixed profit share is agreed upon, ruling that the managing partner bears the loss up to that specific profit amount. Shaykh al-Tusi contextualizes this by explaining that the term 'mudarabah' is used here either metaphorically or to validate a partnership structure where capital is effectively treated as shared, thereby harmonizing this report with earlier hadiths. This highlights the Shia juristic approach to reconciling apparent contradictions in commercial transactions through precise definitional nuances.
